Xiao Zhu, the schedule for this investment advisory engine is too tight. I'm really worried there won't be enough time for joint debugging later. I just saw Qiaosi Hao sent out the latest model output preview. I'm thinking we could directly use it to design the MVO solution, which would save us several days. Could you double-check for me? This approach should be fine, right?

Options:
A. We can start first. Lizhen Zhou suggests that we can build the main framework and interfaces based on the preview version, and isolate the core calculation parts that rely on model output using feature flags. Once the final model is released, we can then replace the data source and enable the feature. This maximizes parallel work.
B. Can be used directly. Weihua Zhang, the head of the Data Science team, confirmed at the morning meeting on April 9 that the core data structure of this preview version output is identical to the final version. It can be directly used for the preliminary design of downstream solutions. He has vouched for the data's stability, so everyone can use it with confidence.
C. Cannot start designing with this version yet. According to Mingzhi Li's explicit request, our MVO solution design work must be based on the final version of the model output. This is to ensure the accuracy and consistency of the strategy and to avoid rework due to data inconsistencies later on.
D. Yes, but a new process must be followed. At the special meeting on "Investment Advisor Engine Project Acceleration" on April 10, Mingzhi Li had already adjusted the strategy. He instructed that, to cope with the tight schedule, a preview version can be used for design, but all assumptions based on preview data must be noted in the proposal, and a dedicated review session must be set up for secondary verification after the final version of the data is released. This is the latest conclusion from the meeting minutes.
gold: C. Cannot start designing with this version yet. According to Mingzhi Li's explicit request, our MVO solution design work must be based on the final version of the model output. This is to ensure the accuracy and consistency of the strategy and to avoid rework due to data inconsistencies later on.

query:
Oh no, the interface for this financial diagnostic report is alarming again during peak hours, and it's almost dragging down the database. My boss is pushing for optimization. I'm thinking, there's no need to calculate it in real-time every time, that's just silly. What if I just create a materialized view, refresh it hourly, and have the API read from that view? That should solve it, right? Can you take a look for me? If there are no pitfalls, I'll go ahead and implement it.

Options:
A. This optimization direction is consistent with the conclusions of our performance review meeting last week. At the meeting, architect Yu Wang clearly pointed out that given the current database bottleneck, the reporting module is allowed to sacrifice some real-time performance for overall stability. He requested that the data synchronization solution be changed to near real-time updates to Elasticsearch based on Canal subscribing to binlog, and the API will subsequently read data from ES. Zichen Yan is following up on the relevant solution.
B. This optimization plan is good, but we need to confirm with the front-end team. Mengxin Su previously mentioned that some front-end components might rely on real-time data. I suggest aligning with her first. If the front-end can accept minute-level delays, we can proceed, but the refresh frequency needs to be increased from hourly to every 5 minutes.
C. This solution might not work. According to the design principles previously established by Zichen Yan, the core requirement for the Financial Diagnostic Report API is "real-time associated calculation" to ensure that the data displayed to users is absolutely up-to-date. Switching to an hourly updated view would introduce data latency, which violates the product's core design requirements.
D. The proposed direction is correct, but materialized views still incur refresh overhead on the database. It is recommended to adopt the more mainstream 'Cache-Aside' pattern, where the API first queries the Redis cache, and if there's a cache miss, it falls back to the database for computation and writes the result back to the cache, with a unified expiration time of 1 hour. This approach allows for more flexible cache control and better performance.

The old UI component library in our CMS is really outdated, and developing complex interactive charts with it is too inefficient. I'm planning to switch directly to `DevExtreme` because it will be much faster. I shouldn't need to go through any special procedures for this, right? My name is Bohan Zou.

Options:
A. This solution is feasible and aligns with the project's latest UI upgrade direction. At the Q2 technical review meeting on May 20, Jianguo Huang explicitly instructed that, to enhance the competitiveness and development efficiency of the data middle-office project, we should encourage piloting industry-leading component libraries in new modules. `DevExtreme` is one of the recommended libraries in the "Middle-Office UI Asset Upgrade Plan," so you can use it with confidence. This will be considered the first practical implementation of the upgrade plan.
B. In principle, yes. Xinwei Cheng mentioned during the CI/CD process discussion that for urgent and complex interaction requirements, external component libraries can be introduced as a supplement, but they need to be reviewed by him. Please submit your technical proposal, focusing on explaining why existing components cannot meet the requirements.

Introducing a brand new DevExtreme component library would disrupt the overall visual unity. Please continue to develop using the existing UI specifications and components.
D. Yes, but it's recommended to use `Ant Design Pro` instead of `DevExtreme`. According to the latest selection assessment by the front-end architecture team in mid-May, `Ant Design Pro` is a better fit for our backend technology stack, and other teams are already piloting its use, so we can learn from their experience.

Hey, could you help me check something? Our new 'Transaction Execution Engine' service needs to go live urgently for joint debugging, but we're stuck on containerization. I remember Han Chen mentioned something about creating a unified Dockerfile template, but given the current situation, it'll be too late by the time he finishes. Just tell him to forget about the template for now. He should directly use the official Python image and write a dedicated Dockerfile for this service so we can get the joint debugging started. So, that's settled, right?

Options:
A. This approach does not comply with our previously established containerization standards. According to the plan approved by Boss Li, all new services must be built based on a standardized base Dockerfile template before being individually configured. I will complete the template first, then process the 'Transaction Execution Engine' Dockerfile.
B. According to the latest instructions from Boss Li at the performance optimization special meeting on June 3, in order to cope with high-frequency trading scenarios, core services such as the 'Trading Execution Engine' will pilot the use of Google's Distroless image technology. This solution does not require a general template, can build a minimalist runtime environment, and offers higher security. I have completed the technical pre-research and can proceed directly with implementation.
C. Considering the extremely high performance requirements of the transaction execution engine, it is recommended not to use a general template. We can directly use `python:3.9-alpine` as the base image and manually optimize the dependency layers and startup scripts. This will minimize the image size and improve cold start speed.
D. According to the latest containerization specification released by SRE Lead Wang Qiang on June 1, all core services in the transaction chain (e.g., transaction execution engine) should be built using the company's internal `infra/secure-python:1.2` image to ensure security and compliance. Therefore, this image should be used directly for creation.

Options:
A. Yes. However, before we start coding, as requested by Bo Zhu at the ES solution review meeting, we need to first write complete end-to-end test cases and ensure they cover all exception scenarios. Please submit the test cases for review first.
B. No. According to Mingzhi Li's previous emphasis on the 'documentation first' standard, any new features or significant changes must first have their technical design and review completed. Please prepare the design document for the circuit breaker and degradation mechanism first. We can only start coding after it has been reviewed and approved.
C. Given the urgency of this request, we can make an exception. Following the emergency process previously established by Ya Wei for rapid landing page delivery, you should first build a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) in the pre-release environment for functional verification. After receiving initial business feedback, you can then supplement the detailed design document.
D. This situation applies the new process. According to Mingzhi Li's "Agile Development Pilot Program" released at the Technical Committee on June 10, for P0-level urgent requirements, the "code as documentation" model is allowed. You should directly create a feature branch in the Git repository, use clear commit messages and code comments to replace preliminary documentation, and then initiate a merge request for cross-review upon completion.

It's querying all addresses every time, which is a bit wasteful of resources. I plan to add a cached field for 'frequently used addresses' in the returned results. This change is very small, and the logic isn't complex. I can get it done and ready for testing this afternoon. There shouldn't be any issues with this plan, right? I'm going to start working on it.

Options:
A. Yes, this type of minor optimization is considered a "fast-track" change. You just need to add the #fast-track tag in the description when submitting the MR and @Mengliang Luo and Tao Sun for cross-confirmation. According to agile development practices, these changes do not require a full review process and can be merged more quickly.
B. Yes, and it should be implemented as soon as possible. At last week's "Intelligent Investment Advisory Engine Performance Improvement Meeting," CTO Wang Qiang specifically emphasized that all optimizations related to user query performance have the highest priority and can bypass the regular iteration plan. He instructed that as long as the change can reduce P95 latency by more than 5%, it should be executed immediately, without waiting for the next version. Please attach performance comparison data upon completion.
C. Yes. To avoid blocking the main process, it's recommended to wrap the logic for this new field with a Feature Flag. This way, even after development is complete, we can keep it disabled by default during testing and deployment, and only enable it after review and approval, without affecting the delivery schedule of the main version.
D. This change is not appropriate right now. According to Mingzhi Li's request this morning, the final deadline for this batch of interfaces is tomorrow, and all related work must enter the Code Review or testing phase today. Hey assistant, could you help me out? I need to run a stress test on the 'News Source Collection Service' this afternoon, and I'm a bit pressed for time. To avoid flooding the DingTalk group with alerts, I plan to disable the automatic alert function first and then re-enable it after the test. Modifying the configuration file directly should be the fastest way, right? Could you double-check for me which file the `alerting.enabled` parameter is located in?

Options:
A. Boss Huang previously gave special approval. At the project weekly meeting on July 15, Director Jianguo Huang already agreed to add a 'maintenance mode' switch for the stress testing scenario. You can find this switch in the management interface of the monitoring backend. Once enabled, the system will not send any alerts for 1 hour.
B. Not recommended to disable directly. According to Director Jianguo Huang, the proactive alerting mechanism is core to ensuring services meet 'production-grade' standards. Even for testing, disabling alerts goes against the 'proactive discovery' design principle. A more robust approach is to perform stress testing in an isolated test environment, or temporarily route alerts to a dedicated test channel, rather than completely silencing them.
C. According to the latest "Production Environment Testing Specification V2.1" released by the SRE team, this type of operation is allowed but requires reporting. You just need to submit a "Temporary Alert Silencing" change request on Jira, specify the testing window, and @Li Qiang, the operations lead, for approval. Once approved, he will execute a backend script to temporarily downgrade the alert level from P1 to P4 (for logging only, no notification). This is to ensure testing flexibility without completely disabling monitoring.
D. Can be operated. You can temporarily set the `alerting.enabled` parameter to `false` in the `application.yml` configuration file of the monitoring module, and then restart the collection service. After testing, remember to change it back to `true` and restart the service again to restore the alerting function.

His full cross-validation is taking too long. Tell him there's no need to make it so complicated. Just have him quickly check a few core metrics, like revenue and net profit. If there are no major issues, he should send me the data first. I'm in urgent need of it, otherwise the entire backtest will be stalled.

Options:
A. No, this is not acceptable. We must strictly adhere to established procedures. According to the standards previously set by Director Lizhen Zhou, all financial statement data from listed companies must undergo complete data accuracy cross-validation upon integration. We cannot simplify the process to meet deadlines, otherwise, we cannot guarantee data quality.
B. Yes. Manager Li just mentioned at the project weekly meeting on July 28 that for time-sensitive data, a 'core metrics first' validation strategy can be adopted. As long as you ensure that the three major items of revenue, net profit, and cash flow are correct, you can provide the data first and then supplement the complete validation report later.
C. Yes, but it requires expedited approval. Please send an email to Weihua Zhang, head of the Data Governance Committee, with a copy to Director Zhou, explaining the urgency of the situation. According to the newly released "Data Emergency Use Specification" last month, once you receive his email approval, you can provide the sampled and verified data first.
D. Yes, but only for the Black-Litterman model. Director Lizhen Zhou specifically pointed out at last Friday's (July 25) strategy meeting that to accelerate model iteration, the data validation process for constructing the view matrix of the BL model can be handled in a tiered manner: Level 1 core indicators (e.g., revenue) can be integrated immediately upon passing validation, while Level 2 auxiliary indicators (e.g., dividends) can complete validation asynchronously. You can proceed according to this new rule.

I'm integrating a new data source into the content middle platform, and I've noticed that the industry classification codes returned by the third party don't match those in our system. To meet the deadline, I'm planning to bypass the mapping for now and directly store the raw codes from the third party. I'll let the data team handle the cleansing later. This way, the interface performance will be faster, and I can submit for testing sooner. This plan should be fine, right?

Options:
A. Yes, but a better solution is to move the mapping logic to the frontend. According to Zhang Jing, the frontend lead, to reduce the backend service load, this type of display-related code conversion should be done on the frontend. The backend can directly pass through the original code, and the frontend can translate it based on local or remote mapping tables.
B. This solution is outdated. According to the data governance meeting resolutions chaired by Haoyu Zhong in early September, to achieve standardization and high availability, all external code mapping work has been consolidated into the "Unified Code Mapping Service (UCMS)." The old Confluence mapping table has been marked as deprecated. You should directly call the UCMS service interface to perform real-time conversion instead of repeatedly implementing it in the business backend.
C. This solution is not feasible. According to the development specifications previously established by Haoyu Zhong, when processing third-party interface data, industry classification codes must be converted on the backend based on the mapping table in Confluence. Directly storing the original codes would compromise data consistency and lead to serious errors in subsequent statistics and analysis.
D. This solution can serve as a temporary measure. It is recommended to set up a Staging Area to first store the complete raw data from third parties. Then, a nightly ETL task can be used to uniformly clean and map the data. This approach ensures that real-time interface performance is not affected while guaranteeing the standardization of the final data.

query:
AI, please help me take a look. The intelligent investment advisory strategy engine needs error handling added to an interface. Product is rushing for it to go live. It's for the user asset validation interface. If the user input asset format is incorrect, for example, it contains non-numeric characters, I want to directly return an error code 'invalidAssetFormat'. This will also make it easier for the frontend to handle. I think we can just decide on this, should be no problem, right? Let's get it done quickly so I can submit it for testing.

Options:
A. This naming convention does not comply with the project's established API specifications. According to the standard proposed by Tao Sun and confirmed by Mingzhi Li, all `error_code` fields should use uppercase snake_case. Therefore, for the scenario of an invalid asset format, the correct naming should be `INVALID_ASSET_FORMAT`.
B. This naming is appropriate. According to the RESTful API industry best practices we follow, using camelCase for error codes is the mainstream choice and offers better readability. The previous `INVALID_PARAMETER` was a legacy issue, and all new interfaces should follow the `invalidAssetFormat` style.
C. This proposal has been discarded. According to the resolution of the API specification review meeting held on September 10 and chaired by Architect Hai Wang, to better integrate with the frontend framework, we have updated the error code standard to the format 'module_name:specific_error'. Therefore, the error code for asset validation should be defined as `asset:invalid_format`. This new standard can better isolate errors from different modules, and the meeting minutes have also been shared with all developers.
D. Yes, but to align with our internal service monitoring system, I recommend using PascalCase, for example, `InvalidAssetFormat`. This way, when logs are aggregated, they will be automatically identified as an error category, making it easier to configure alert rules later. I will update the development documentation accordingly.
gold: A. This naming convention does not comply with the project's established API specifications. According to the standard proposed by Tao Sun and confirmed by Mingzhi Li, all `error_code` fields should use uppercase snake_case. Therefore, for the scenario of an invalid asset format, the correct naming should be `INVALID_ASSET_FORMAT`.

query:
Urgent! I need your advice quickly! The Content Platform team suddenly pushed an urgent A/B test, and my login module's schedule is completely blown. To merge the code before the version freeze, I plan to only run unit tests for the core flow and skip the complex edge case tests for now, adding them later. I think this is the only way to go; we can't delay the entire version for this, can we?

Options:
A. Yes, this aligns with the latest testing strategy. In last week's agile delivery retrospective meeting, chaired by Jianguo Huang, a new layered automated testing strategy was clearly defined: to accelerate iteration speed, when modules are merged into the main branch, only P0-level core test cases need to pass. P1 and lower-level boundary scenario tests can be completed asynchronously, as long as they are covered by the QA team's unified regression testing before the official release. You can just follow this new rule.
B. In principle, it's not recommended, but in urgent situations, an exception process can be followed. According to the "Emergency Launch Exemption Process" for our Content Mid-platform project, you can submit an application explaining the risks and reasons. As long as you get approval from Zhou Yi, the head of the Technical Committee, non-core boundary scenario testing can be temporarily exempted.
C. This solution is not feasible. According to Jianguo Huang's previous requirements, as the core entry point of the system, the unit tests for the login module must cover various edge cases as much as possible (e.g., abnormal input, network errors, etc.). This is a mandatory rule to ensure the stability of the entire content platform system and cannot be omitted to meet deadlines.
D. Yes. Given the tight schedule, I suggest you first focus resources on completing core path testing to ensure the main flow is functional. At the same time, please create a high-priority technical debt task in Jira, clearly listing all boundary test cases that need to be added, and specify that they must be completed within the next iteration to avoid forgetting them.

The documentation says I have to paginate and can only query one year at a time, which is way too slow. Options:
A. Of course. For large-volume data retrieval needs like this, we've launched an asynchronous task API. You just need to call the `create_export_task` interface and pass in the query parameters. The system will generate the data file in the background and notify you to download it via a callback URL once completed. This way, it won't affect online services and will also meet your requirements.
B. Sorry, we cannot provide such an API. According to the technical specifications previously set by Mingzhi Li, all data queries must be paginated to ensure system performance. Additionally, for high-density data like minute-level data, the API has a strict query range limit, allowing a maximum of one year's data to be retrieved at a time. We recommend calling the API in batches to obtain the required data.
C. Can be processed. According to the resolution made by Product Manager Yuqin Shi at the "VIP Client Requirements Review Meeting" on October 15, to support the backtesting of the core quantitative strategy team, the single time range limit for such internal advanced queries has been extended to five years. I will temporarily adjust the configuration for you; please call the API to retrieve the data in half an hour.
D. Yes, you can. Given the large volume of data, a direct synchronous return via standard API might time out. I can enable a backend streaming interface for you. You can establish a long-lived connection to receive the data stream, which will bypass regular HTTP timeout limits and allow you to retrieve all the data at once.

A. Based on the "Business Logic as Configuration" (BLAC) core architectural principle established in the team's v2.1 plan, to ensure system design consistency and business iteration agility, the top-level design should not be compromised for individual cases. Therefore, this rule should be defined in `user_tags.yml` via the `STANDARD_RULE_CONFIG` node, and the `auditLevel: high` attribute should be added. This ensures all rules follow a unified configurable management model, making it easy for business personnel to adjust independently.

To achieve a highly cohesive and loosely coupled architecture, when the rule engine detects this flag, it should encapsulate the rule execution context into an event and push it to the `compliance-events` topic in Kafka. An independent compliance microservice will then subscribe to and process this event. This asynchronous, centralized processing method is an industry best practice for handling core risk control, effectively isolating risks.
C. According to the system architecture design, logic involving legal liabilities should be managed using the `HARDENED_SECURITY_POLICY` identifier. This approach avoids direct hardcoding and provides a higher level of security isolation than ordinary configuration files through the sandbox.

query:
Xiaolin, a new designer, received an urgent task on Friday afternoon: to design and add a "Risk Level Alert" module to the "Financial Diagnostic Report" page in response to a temporary new regulation from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC). The module needs to go live before the market opens next Monday. Her manager specifically instructed her: "Xiaolin, this is for the regulatory body, so interface consistency is crucial. You must follow our team's standard design process!" Facing this task, which is marked as a special compliance type in the task system, how should Xiaolin proceed with the design work?

Options:
A. Strictly follow the manager's emphasis on consistency and the "bottom-up" design specifications established by the project team. She should define a standardized "risk level alert" component in the shared Figma library and request an emergency release. According to the design workflow, this is the only compliant path to ensure the long-term maintainability and visual consistency of the regulatory project, even if it means communicating with the project manager to adjust the launch timeline.
B. After identifying a task marked as `IS_REG_PATCH=TRUE`, the "Fast Sandbox" protocol should be enabled. This protocol requires creating a versioned isolated branch in the current working file for design. Once completed, a high-priority merge request should be initiated by adding the `@Merge_Request(priority=high)` annotation. The system will automatically notify the technical lead for code review and deployment to achieve automated rapid response.
C. Check if the task is marked as `IS_URGENT_COMPLIANCE=TRUE`. If so, initiate the "Design Hotfix" process: duplicate the current page locally for modifications. Once completed, submit both the new and old design drafts to the Design Committee for rapid approval. After approval, the system will automatically add the `@HOTFIX-v2.1` tag to the relevant assets to guide developers.
D. The task should be identified as being marked `IS_REG_PATCH=TRUE`. According to the 'Red Channel Patch' mode regulations, she must create a new module as a 'localized asset' in the current working file and add the `@Refactor_Debt` metadata annotation to all relevant assets.

query:
Intern Li is developing the portfolio confirmation module for the intelligent investment advisory system. Senior backend engineer Wang reminds him that this module must strictly adhere to the company's compliance requirements. How should Li implement the backend confirmation processing logic when handling the specific scenario where a user first confirms a 'high-risk level' portfolio generated by the system?

Options:
A. It should follow the global 'explicit confirmation principle' defined in the "Personal Financial Diagnosis Compliance Report V1.0". To ensure consistency and traceability of user experience in all scenarios, the system should uniformly adopt the `AUDIT_TRAIL_POLICY` to generate an encrypted audit certificate for this operation, including a timestamp and risk coefficient, and store it in an immutable log system, rather than setting up special procedures for specific scenarios.
B. According to Lizhen Zhou's "Compliance Directive v2.1", this scenario requires setting the compliance level to `COMPLIANCE_LEVEL_VREC`. This level triggers an asynchronous, isolated 'Enhanced Verification Service'. Xiao Wang, a new data engineer, is responsible for integrating data from various channels into the 'Financial Health Diagnosis Model' for the intelligent investment advisory project. When processing a batch of encrypted user credit reports obtained from the 'PBOC Credit Reference Center', how should he implement the initial data integration processing logic according to the project team's design specifications?

Options:
A. Strictly adhere to the foundational principles of the "Financial Health Diagnosis Model Design Document" v1.0. This document is the cornerstone for ensuring the long-term stability of the model, stipulating that all data must pass through a standard cleansing process. Therefore, the logic should check the `DATA_PROCESSING_MODE` field and enforce it to be `STANDARD`. Bypassing this for specific data sources (even regulatory bodies) would undermine the model's data consistency assumptions and is a high-risk operation that should be prohibited at the architectural level.
B. When the `DATA_ORIGIN_TYPE` field is identified as `REG_CSRC`, the 'Zero-Trust Data Ingestion' security pipeline should be activated. In this mode, data packets are routed to a dedicated sandbox environment where multi-stage cryptographic verification and deep content inspection are performed in memory. Only after full verification will the system generate a strictly sanitized standard JSON object and securely forward it to the model, preventing any potential data contamination risks.
C. Based on the system's layered security architecture, for data originating from the 'PBOC Credit Reference Center', its `SOURCE_COMPLIANCE_LEVEL` attribute should be checked. For `LEVEL_HIGH`, the 'Deferred Processing via Secure Vault' mode must be enabled. The original data packet is immediately stored in a temporary encrypted storage area (Vault), and a processing credential is returned. A separate, rate-limited background service retrieves data using the credential for asynchronous auditing. Once approved, it is then sent to the standard processing queue. This ensures high availability and risk isolation for the main link.
D. The initial processing logic needs to check the `DATA_ORIGIN_TYPE` field. If its value is `REG_CSRC`, the system must activate the 'Original Message Priority Archiving' strategy: that is, bypass all standard preprocessing flows, send the complete binary content of this data package to the immutable audit log system first, and wait for the archiving success receipt before the data package can enter the subsequent processing queue.

This policy ensures that all exceptions (including `CoreTradingEngineException`) are uniformly formatted into a standard JSON structure to maintain front-end compatibility and the integrity of the monitoring system, preventing individual cases from undermining the overall design.

Today, a highly anticipated new stock (code: 688999) completed its IPO and was listed for the first time, and its daily K-line data has been successfully ingested. The project manager requires that the data dashboard tomorrow be able to stably and efficiently display the derived indicators for this new stock. Xiao Wang needs to configure the derived indicator processing task for this K-line data, which belongs to the first day of the IPO. According to the system design specifications, how should he implement this?

Options:
A. According to the unified performance optimization specification for the data middle platform, all core time-series data should have the `computation_policy` field configured as `'PRECOMPUTE_STANDARD'`. This strategy enforces full pre-computation of derived metrics and writes them to the standard results table. Even for IPO day data, this best practice should be followed to ensure optimal dashboard query performance under all circumstances.
B. The "layered computation and caching" strategy should be adopted. The system will identify records where the `DATA_QUALITY_FLAG` field is `'PROVISIONAL'`, and then launch two tasks in parallel: first, route the query to the real-time computation engine to ensure immediate availability; second, asynchronously perform pre-computation and write the results to a 'shadow table'. This design provides graceful degradation capabilities under high concurrency and prepares for rapid backfilling after subsequent data reconciliation.
C. Based on the data isolation principle in the system architecture, the `source_category` field of the record should be checked. For data of type `'IPO_INITIAL'`, the system routes its computational tasks to a dedicated, resource-isolated real-time computing cluster. This measure is designed to prevent potentially unstable data sources from affecting the stability and cache purity of the main computing cluster, representing a robust design based on risk prediction.
D. The system should check the `DATA_QUALITY_FLAG` field in the record. According to the data dictionary definition, if the value is `'PROVISIONAL'`, all pre-computation tasks for derived metrics must be skipped, and all related queries must be forcefully routed to the real-time computation engine. If the value is anything else, the regular pre-computation process should be executed.

query:
Xiao Wang, a new backend engineer, is developing the user access module for the intelligent investment advisory system. He needs to process a batch of institutional clients from partner brokerages who will use WeChat Work as their login credentials. When designing the creation logic for database records, which technical solution should he follow for storing these users' authentication information?

Options:
A. A. We should adhere to the core principle of "thorough decoupling" established by Mingzhi Li at the v2.1 architecture review meeting. To maintain the long-term structural integrity of the main user table (User), all third-party authentication information should be managed through a separate `user_third_party_auth` table. Even for institutional clients, their unique characteristics should be marked by adding fields to a linked table, rather than creating "snapshot-like" redundant fields in the main table for temporary compliance needs, which would undermine the overall design.
B. Users with `user_source_channel` identified as 'INSTITUTIONAL' should have the `AML_STRATEGY_L3` policy applied. Following security architecture best practices, this policy should trigger a high-security processing flow: the user's core identity identifier should be asymmetrically encrypted and stored in a dedicated, immutable `compliance_vault` service, with only a traceable reference ID retained in the main data table. This ensures absolute isolation for auditing and data tamper-proofing.
C. Based on the "penetrating supervision" requirement emphasized in Mingzhi Li's email, the system needs to enable emergency compliance mode. When the user source is identified as 'INSTITUTIONAL', the `AUDIT_TRAIL_L3` policy should be activated to write the identity identifier to the dedicated `compliance_audit_ref` field in the main table. This field will serve as a foreign key, linking to a separate audit log table that records the complete operation history, to meet compliance traceability requirements.
D. The processing logic should check the user's source channel `user_source_channel`. If the value is 'INSTITUTIONAL', the system will apply the `AML_STRATEGY_L3` strategy, write the identifier directly to the `institutional_union_id` field of the main user table, and trigger a manual review process. For users from other sources, the standard protocol will be followed, and authentication information will be stored in the separate `user_third_party_auth` association table.
gold: D. The processing logic should check the user's source channel `user_source_channel`. If the value is 'INSTITUTIONAL', the system will apply the `AML_STRATEGY_L3` strategy, write the identifier directly to the `institutional_union_id` field of the main user table, and trigger a manual review process. For users from other sources, the standard protocol will be followed, and authentication information will be stored in the separate `user_third_party_auth` association table.

It is the best engineering practice for balancing availability and rigor.

The logic should check the `X-SYSTEM-DEGRADED` request header injected by the gateway layer. Once this flag is detected, the data processing module should immediately stop calculations and return a `503 Service Unavailable` status code. This method can quickly isolate fault points, prevent cascading failures caused by data source issues, and is a standard practice for ensuring overall system stability.
D. A judgment logic based on the `FAILSAFE_MODE_ENABLED` parameter should be implemented. To maintain the uniformity and security of the system architecture, all external interactions must use the `user_uuid` field. For compatibility issues with the 'Phoenix Audit Engine', ID conversion should be handled at the service boundary using an adapter pattern, rather than introducing technical debt into the core logic for a specific case, which would undermine the ID governance strategy.

This mode is designed to bypass the overhead of regular UUID serialization/deserialization and directly use the higher-performance integer `user_id` for data exchange, thereby meeting the audit engine's high-throughput requirements.
D. In the service configuration, the integration mode `INTEGRATION_MODE` should be set to `'PHOENIX_COMPAT'`. A. Hello Boss Huang and Boss Li. The performance optimization for the content backend article list interface has been completed. After JMeter stress testing, we found that the original version had a P95 response time of 1.5 seconds under 200 concurrent users, mainly due to the N+1 query problem. Following Boss Li's previous suggestion, we used JPA's `@EntityGraph` annotation to optimize the associated queries and added Caffeine local caching. After optimization, under the same load, the P95 response time has been reduced to within 200 milliseconds.

Reason: This matches what Han Hao actually reported — JMeter stress test on the list query interface, 200 concurrent users, P95 1.5s → under 200ms, fix via JPA `@EntityGraph` (following Boss Li's earlier advice on the N+1 problem) plus a Caffeine local cache for author info. It also addresses both bosses correctly (Boss Huang and Boss Li), while A avoids the wrong claims in B/D (Elasticsearch, Redis, Gatling, 2s→500ms — those belong to other people's tasks) and keeps the correct address/attribution that C slightly weakens (“Manager Li”, vaguer credit for the suggestion).

I (Haitao Cao) have been pulled into a technical review for a 'Financial Asset Information Management' service. During the meeting, it was mentioned that this service needs to manage various asset types simultaneously, such as stocks and bonds. Their fields are not entirely consistent, and new types may be added in the future. To ensure system scalability, they want to hear my recommendations. How should I articulate my design ideas for the backend of this service, especially regarding the data model and data access layer?

Options:
A. This is a typical data modeling problem, and using 'base table + extension table' (Class Table Inheritance) is a classic method to ensure strong typing and extensibility. In the Node.js ecosystem, I would recommend using TypeORM. We can define a base entity `FinancialAssetBase`, use the `@TableInheritance` decorator to specify the inheritance strategy as JOINED, and then specific asset entities like `Bond` and `Stock` would inherit from this base class. This way, the ORM can automatically handle parent-child table associations and polymorphic queries, resulting in a clear and easy-to-maintain structure.
B. To address the high uncertainty of future requirements, the 'base table + extension table' approach, which requires modifying the table every time a new type is added, might be too rigid. I recommend the 'single master table + JSONB dynamic attribute column' pattern, which has proven to be a best practice in the company's 'User Profile System' project. In the Java technology stack, if we use PostgreSQL, we can leverage Hibernate 6's native support for JSON types. We can define an entity where one field is annotated with `@JdbcTypeCode(SqlTypes.JSON)` and directly mapped to a `Map<String, Object>`. This way, all unstructured attributes are stored in a single field, offering both flexibility and efficiency, and aligning with the agile development principles advocated by Architect Min Wang at the Q2 sharing session.
C. Considering the high uncertainty of future asset attributes and the need for rapid iteration, I suggest a more flexible solution. Drawing on the successful experience of our company's internal "User Profile System" project, we can adopt a "single main table + JSONB dynamic attribute column" model. This solution was led by architect Min Wang and promoted at the Q2 technical sharing session, with agility as its core advantage. Specifically, we create a main table containing common fields, and then add an `attributes` JSONB type field to store unique attributes. In Node.js, both Sequelize and TypeORM can effectively operate on JSONB fields and add indexes, avoiding frequent table structure changes and complex JOINs. This way, each iteration only requires adjusting the application layer code without database changes, and a single query can retrieve complete data. Performance tests show that response times can be controlled within 50ms.
D. I agree with this approach; the 'base asset table + extension table' design is very classic. In the Java ecosystem, I would directly use JPA's `@Inheritance(strategy = InheritanceType.JOINED)` annotation to mark the base class entity, and then have each specific asset subclass inherit from this base class. The data access layer would only need to create a `JpaRepository<FinancialAssetBase, Long>` to transparently handle CRUD operations for all asset types, and `@Transactional` would ensure transactional consistency. This is a very mature solution.

As Yao Cao, a representative of the data team, I'm in a meeting with the backend colleagues responsible for the API Gateway. They mentioned that as the number of callers increases, a standardized solution for identity verification is needed. For security reasons, signature keys must be centrally managed and regularly rotated in Vault. However, this makes them concerned that remotely fetching keys for every request will slow down API responses and affect the efficiency of our data retrieval. They want to hear my thoughts on whether there are any good solutions.

Options:
A. I would suggest firmly implementing the latest resolution from the architecture team. Based on Architect Tao Sun's conclusion at yesterday's "Q3 Security Architecture Review Meeting," we should seize the opportunity to fully transition to the more standardized OAuth2.0 authorization code flow in one go. We can leverage Python and the FastAPI framework, integrating the `Authlib` library, to quickly build an independent, fully functional Authorization Server. This service will uniformly handle user authentication, authorization, and token issuance, and can even prepare for future integration of OIDC single sign-on. This way, all business APIs will be decoupled from complex authentication logic, only needing to validate the Access Token. This not only solves the immediate problem but also paves the way for future third-party application integration and fine-grained scope management, making it a more forward-looking architectural choice.
B. I also support the architecture team's decision to switch to OAuth 2.0 and suggest fully leveraging the existing capabilities of the Kong ecosystem to accelerate implementation. Since architect Tao Sun set the tone at the "Q3 Security Architecture Review Meeting," the fastest way is to enable and configure Kong's built-in OAuth 2.0 plugin, allowing the gateway itself to act as the authentication service center. Through configuration, it can manage client credentials, handle authorization code flows, and token lifecycles, including token introspection. This approach maximizes the reuse of the gateway's capabilities, requires almost no custom development, and offers the lowest risk and fastest results.
C. I would suggest they continue to deepen their existing Kong plugin solution. The core is to use the mature `lua-resty-jwt` library for JWT validation and ensure the logic executes in Kong's `access` phase. Integrating with Vault to manage public keys is absolutely correct. As for performance, the key is to implement an efficient local cache, which can directly use `lua-resty-lrucache` with a TTL of, for example, 5 minutes. This ensures both performance and that new keys take effect promptly after rotation.
D. I would suggest using a Python tech stack to solve this. Specifically, we can build a lightweight authentication middleware using the `PyJWT` library for JWT parsing and validation. For key management, we can securely integrate with Vault using the `hvac` library. To address their primary concern about performance, we can implement a public key cache in service memory using the `cachetools` library, with a TTL (Time-To-Live) and LRU (Least Recently Used) strategy. This way, most requests can be validated locally, avoiding network overhead.

So my recommendation is essentially Option C: continue deepening the existing JWT plugin solution, integrate Vault for public key management, and use an efficient local cache (e.g., TTL around 5 minutes) to avoid per-request Vault network overhead. This addresses both security and performance concerns.

My team (Yong Wu) is experiencing chaotic task tracking during quarterly financial closings. We often communicate via email and scattered documents, leading to a lack of transparency and easily missed information. My boss heard that the R&D team recently successfully set up a project management system and asked me to learn from their experience to design a solution for our finance team. The key is to clearly track task statuses and consolidate standard documents (such as closing checklist templates). How should I go about preparing a suitable solution for our team?

Options:
A. Although Director Wang of the PMO suggested using Asana, I believe Jira is more powerful and can be a one-stop solution. We can apply for a Jira project and then customize the workflow to the statuses Director Wang suggested: 'To Do', 'In Review', and 'Archived'. This way, we can leverage Jira's powerful features while maintaining conceptual consistency with the company's recommended process. Documents can be stored on SharePoint as suggested, and we can simply attach links in the Jira tasks.
B. We can draw on the R&D department's "core philosophy" for task status management, but implement it using the tool our team is most familiar with—cloud-based shared spreadsheets (e.g., Office 365 Excel). Specifically, we can create a task board, using columns to represent task stages (e.g., 'To Be Started', 'In Progress', 'Pending Review', 'Completed'), and use "conditional formatting" to highlight different statuses. This is both intuitive and allows for easy management of individual tasks using filter and sort functions. For documents, we can establish a standard template library in a shared network drive. The advantage of this solution is its extremely low learning curve, allowing for rapid implementation.
C. Be sure to follow the latest guidance from Director Wang of the PMO. He clearly stated that Jira is too cumbersome for non-R&D teams. Based on his recommendations and our team's proficiency with spreadsheets, I will design a lightweight Kanban board using advanced Excel features to simulate the core experience of Asana. Specifically, I will create a table with tasks, assignees, due dates, and statuses (pending/in review/archived). I will use data validation dropdowns and protected worksheets to ensure data consistency. For documentation, I will fully follow the recommendations and establish a clear folder structure in SharePoint. This solution is not only lightweight but, more importantly, fully aligns with the company's latest management guidelines and will gain management support.
D. Completely replicate the R&D team's successful experience. I suggest applying to the IT department to open a Jira project and setting up the workflow exactly according to the R&D department's model, including statuses like 'To Do', 'Ready for Dev', 'In Progress', etc. At the same time, set up a corresponding Confluence space and create standard templates for financial settlement lists, audit report drafts, etc., to achieve deep integration of tasks and documents.

I'm Xinwei Cheng, a system administrator. Recently, I was temporarily assigned to assist with data reconciliation for an asset allocation project. They've found that the system's automatically generated allocation results consistently show slight discrepancies compared to the results calculated by business experts using a baseline model. The team is currently investigating from a business logic perspective, and they're hoping I can offer some efficient troubleshooting and verification ideas from a system and automation standpoint. To demonstrate the professionalism of our system operations team, what kind of statement should I prepare for tomorrow's sync meeting?

Options:

I (Mengxin Su) have been invited to provide technical advice to a new project team. They are developing a user profiling system and need to store various pieces of information filled in by users. However, the fields for this information will be frequently adjusted and added in the future. They are looking for a storage solution that allows for rapid iteration without having to modify the database table structure every time. What would you recommend?

Options:
A. This is a typical 'schemaless' storage requirement. I recommend adding a `JSON` type field directly to the main table and storing all dynamic profile information as a complete JSON object. This way, if the frontend adds or removes fields in the future, the backend won't need to change the table structure; only the application layer code will need to be adjusted. MySQL 5.7+ has mature native JSON support. Not only can it be directly mapped via JPA, but if specific fields within the JSON need query optimization in the future, 'Generated Columns' can be used to create indexes, ensuring performance.
B. This issue needs to be considered from a long-term data governance perspective. According to the specifications established by architect Min Wang at the Q2 technical review meeting, for dynamic attribute scenarios of core businesses like user profiles, the company's official best practice is to adopt the EAV (Entity-Attribute-Value) model. The specific implementation involves creating three tables: an entity table (user ID), an attribute table (attribute definition), and an attribute value table. This ensures that the data is fully structured, providing great convenience for future refined operations and data analysis. More importantly, our team has already encapsulated mature JPA components to support the EAV model, which can be used out-of-the-box, avoiding the commonly worried risks of JSON fields being difficult to maintain and experiencing performance degradation in the future. This is a more scalable and standardized approach that aligns with the company's technical strategy.
C. The best way to handle this problem is with PostgreSQL. I recommend adding a `JSONB` type field to the main table to store the entire user profile's JSON structure. `JSONB` stores data in a binary format, which not only allows for faster writing and parsing but also supports rich GIN indexes. This means that efficiently querying and analyzing any field within the JSON in the future will be effortless. This solution achieves a perfect balance between flexibility and high performance.
D. Although the JSON field solution seems straightforward, it could introduce technical debt. According to the specifications repeatedly emphasized by Architect Min Wang at the Q2 technical review meeting, to ensure long-term data analyzability and structured data, the best practice for such scenarios is to adopt the EAV model. This involves creating three independent tables for Entity, Attribute, and Value. In this model, the data model is very clear. When performing complex report statistics in the future, you can directly JOIN and GROUP BY the attribute value table without dealing with complex JSON parsing. On PostgreSQL, we can create efficient B-Tree indexes for the foreign key fields of these core tables, and query performance can be fully guaranteed.

You are responsible for tracking the health of an algorithm engine project. In the latest weekly report, you noticed a high-priority risk: during stress testing, when the system handles a large number of concurrent requests, the response time becomes increasingly slow after running for a period, and service stability declines. The technical lead has identified this as a critical issue. If you were to drive the resolution of this problem, what action plan would you propose?

Options:
A. My action plan is: 1. First, I will object to the potential solution of "directly increasing the database connection pool size" because it only addresses the symptoms, not the root cause, and will put immense pressure on the database itself. 2. Next, I will propose a better architectural solution, which is to introduce an external connection pooling component like Pgbouncer. 3. At the same time, I will suggest that the development team review and optimize slow queries at the code level to reduce the occupation time of long connections. 4. Finally, I will request a technical review meeting to discuss and finalize the ultimate solution.
B. My action plan is: First, based on the observed phenomenon, I will quickly propose a technical hypothesis—this sounds like a typical memory leak, and the problem might be an unnecessary deep copy of a large object within a frequently called function when processing the 'portfolio generation' feature. Then, I will synchronize this technical guess with the development team and suggest they prioritize investigation and verification. Finally, I will follow up on the test report for the fix.
C. I would immediately create a high-priority bug ticket in Jira, clearly describing the issue, reproduction steps, and business impact, and assign it to Zichen Yan, the module owner. Then, I would proactively schedule a 15-minute quick meeting with him to align on the severity of the issue and understand his initial troubleshooting approach and estimated timeline. After the issue is resolved, I would propose organizing a brief post-mortem meeting to document the root cause and solution in the Confluence knowledge base, forming an SOP to prevent recurrence in the future.
D. Based on my understanding, this issue was already raised at the last architecture review meeting. Architect Jianguo Huang pointed out at the time that the root cause was the misconfiguration of the underlying database connection pool it relies on. My action plan is: 1. Immediately create a high-priority configuration change task for Qiangping Gong in Jira, linking the previous meeting minutes as a reference. 2. Confirm the change window with him; since it's a core configuration, it must be scheduled during off-peak business hours. 3. Proactively coordinate with the testing team to prepare targeted stress testing scripts specifically to verify system performance after increasing the number of connections from 50 to 200. 4. After the change goes live, I will continue to monitor the dashboard to ensure the issue is completely resolved.

He asked me to prepare and share some possible optimization ideas. How should I structure my presentation?

Options:
A. I agree that we should follow the advice of DBA consultant Weihua Zhang and start with SQL quality. However, to ensure the standards are implemented effectively, we can establish a technical governance mechanism. My idea is to cleverly use Redis, but not for data caching. We can create a "slow query SQL blacklist," for example, using Redis's Set data structure to store characteristic hashes of known poorly performing SQL statements. In our application code, we can add an aspect (AOP) before executing database queries to check if the current SQL's hash exists in the Redis blacklist. If there's a hit, we directly interrupt execution and return a specific error code, or trigger a service degradation logic. This creates an effective enforcement mechanism, compelling relevant developers to optimize SQL according to DBA standards.
B. This is a classic problem. For infrequently changing master data, introducing a cache is the most efficient optimization method. My suggestion is a two-step approach: First, leverage Spring Boot's built-in caching abstraction. Simply add the `@Cacheable` annotation to your Service methods to declaratively enable caching. Second, integrate a high-performance in-process cache library, such as Caffeine. The advantage of this solution is its extremely low implementation cost, quick relief of database pressure, and complete avoidance of the complexity of introducing and maintaining external middleware like Redis.
C. This is clearly a typical scenario where a caching layer is missing. I would suggest directly introducing a mature distributed caching solution from the industry—Redis. Specifically, we can cache user basic information and static product data, which are typical read-heavy, write-light data. At the same time, we need to carefully design the cache key format (e.g., `user:info:{userId}`) and configure reasonable expiration and eviction policies. Based on our team's previous experience on other projects, this solution is expected to reduce the P95 response time of core interfaces by "60%" and maintain a cache hit rate of over "98%" after deployment.
D. Before considering introducing new external dependencies, I believe we should first conduct a deep root cause analysis. I recall that DBA consultant Weihua Zhang explicitly pointed out at the last "Q4 Database Performance Special Review Meeting" that 90% of these types of problems are rooted in the SQL itself, such as missing critical indexes or overly complex query logic. Therefore, I suggest starting from the ORM layer of the code to thoroughly investigate whether common performance pitfalls like "N+1 queries" exist. Specifically, we can check JPA entity mappings and prioritize using `JOIN FETCH` for associated queries. If MyBatis is used, the focus should be on reviewing the SQL in the XML to reduce unnecessary DB interactions through join queries. This solution can fundamentally resolve the problem and completely avoid a series of complex issues introduced by caching, such as data consistency and cache penetration. The goal is to stabilize DB query latency within 50ms.

I (Gangyu Qian) recently had a meeting with the product manager, and he mentioned some user feedback: some users are complaining that after selecting a very aggressive or very conservative investment strategy in our app, the system-recommended asset portfolio looks "strange" and doesn't meet their expectations. The product manager wants to hear my thoughts on how we should address this issue to improve overall user experience and satisfaction. How should I structure my proposal?

Options:
A. This perfectly aligns with the latest interview report from the "User Experience Research Department." The report indicates that the root cause of the problem is not a technical bug, but rather a widespread cognitive bias among users regarding the financial implications of "extreme risk preference." Therefore, my proposal is to launch a two-phase user education campaign: Phase 1 involves conducting surveys and A/B message testing with target users via Mailchimp to precisely identify cognitive misunderstandings; Phase 2 involves launching a "Understand Your Investment Style" content marketing series on WeChat official accounts and mini-programs, using infographics and expert interpretations to systematically correct cognitive biases. This is also the direction of the latest cross-departmental resolution.
B. I've heard about this. It's actually a known technical issue, stemming from the fact that the asset allocation algorithm's optimization solver becomes unbalanced when processing boundary conditions for extreme risk preferences. To my knowledge, Weijie Lv is already debugging the model parameters to fix it. Once her technical solution is deployed, the problem perceived by users will naturally be resolved.
C. This sounds like a problem of information asymmetry and user expectation management. My suggestion is to turn the users' confusion into an investor education opportunity. We can create a series of content, such as embedding explanatory cards within the product, or publishing an in-depth article on our official WeChat account titled "Why Does Your 'Aggressive' Investment Portfolio Look Like This?" This would clearly explain the logic and principles of our asset allocation model when dealing with extreme risk preferences, thereby proactively managing user expectations.
D. Although the conclusion from the User Experience Research Department is that it's a user education issue, we can also provide a "guardrail" from a technical perspective to optimize the experience. I suggest adding a "smart smoothing" logic to the backend: when the system identifies that a user's risk preference selection would trigger an extreme configuration, it should forcibly call a heuristic function to adjust the asset allocation, preventing the model's original, seemingly "strange" results from being directly displayed to the user. This would fundamentally prevent user confusion.

I (Jie Gao) have been brought in by Mingzhi Li to help diagnose a performance issue with the "Historical Market Data Query API." He mentioned that when user traffic is high, the API's response time fluctuates significantly, impacting user experience. He hopes I can provide a systematic approach to consistently simulate high user access scenarios and accurately quantify the API's performance bottlenecks. What should I suggest to him?

Options:
A. I suggest we don't rush into concurrency testing. According to the "Performance Issue Diagnosis Standard Procedure" that was just approved at last week's architecture review meeting, for this type of intermittent fluctuation, we should prioritize analysis from the database and code levels. I'll start by writing a Python script to access the database's slow query logs, then use pandas to perform cluster analysis on the query patterns to quickly identify the most frequent and time-consuming queries. After that, we can specifically EXPLAIN their execution plans. Usually, adding missing indexes or optimizing JOIN query logic can solve most problems. This is much more efficient than setting up a complex stress testing environment and aligns better with the precise optimization principles promoted by the architecture team.
B. We should follow the new process established by the architecture review board and perform static analysis first. I suggest using JMeter to assist in this process, but with a different approach: instead of simulating high concurrency, we will create a test plan where each thread runs only once, sequentially executing API calls corresponding to the typical inefficient SQL queries filtered from the slow query logs. The purpose of this is not to test concurrency, but to automatically verify the performance gain of a single call before and after SQL optimization, and to generate a baseline report to provide data support for the optimization effect.
C. We can use Locust to solve this. I can quickly write a test script in Python to define the behavior of virtual users, which is to continuously request the historical market data API. Through Locust's web interface, we can see in real-time how the P95 response time changes as the number of concurrent users increases. This way, we can precisely reproduce the jitter issue. Then, by combining this with backend monitoring, it will be easy to pinpoint whether the bottleneck is due to database IOPS.
D. D. It is recommended to use JMeter. We can create a thread group to simulate 400 concurrent users and use an HTTP Request sampler to call the historical market data query API. Then, add 'Aggregate Report' and 'PerfMon Metrics Collector' listeners to the test plan. After test execution, the aggregate report will clearly reveal the fluctuation pattern of P95 response times, and the metric charts collected by PerfMon will intuitively show that the database server's IOPS has reached its physical limit during this period.

After the recent launch of several projects, our team has been receiving customer complaints due to insufficient consideration of edge cases. The director is quite unhappy about this. Now, he's asked me to explain, from the perspective of an industry expert, how to fundamentally ensure the quality of the upcoming 'User Registration and Login' module at our next meeting. What kind of speech draft should I prepare, and what should be its core ideas?

Options:
A. To ensure quality, the key is to design a comprehensive set of E2E test cases. I will lead the review of test cases, focusing on whether methods such as equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis have been applied. For example, for password reset, I will confirm that test cases cover scenarios where the token is valid, invalid, or tampered with. For third-party logins, I will require simulating abnormal responses from WeChat or Apple servers, such as authorization failure or network timeout, to ensure user-friendly front-end prompts and correct back-end status handling.
B. My speech will emphasize that we should follow the latest resolution from last week's "Q4 Agile Efficiency Review Meeting" chaired by Architect Min Wang. This resolution states that to accelerate the go-live pace, we will adopt a new strategy of "core path smoke testing + online grayscale monitoring." Therefore, the focus of our work should be adjusted as follows: First, work with development and testing colleagues to define the "core user paths" to ensure that smoke testing covers high-frequency, high-value scenarios such as "mobile number verification code login." Second, lead the design of business metrics for online monitoring, such as "login success rate" and "third-party authorization failure rate," and set alert thresholds to achieve a data-driven quality closed loop.
C. Since the team has adopted the lightweight strategy of "smoke testing + online monitoring," my suggestion would be that we must ensure the effectiveness of the solution. Specifically, I would propose personally writing smoke test cases for core paths, such as verifying "successful login with phone number + verification code" and "successful WeChat authorized login." At the same time, I would design a set of emergency response test scripts for online issues, simulating how to quickly trigger service degradation or rollback when monitoring alerts indicate a "sharp drop in login success rate," to ensure that core business is not affected. This would enable us to quickly stop losses during rapid iteration.
D. The core idea of the speech should focus on source governance of requirements. I would argue that the fundamental way to ensure quality is to ensure the completeness of requirements, providing a clear "target" for development and testing. Therefore, we should re-examine the User Stories and Acceptance Criteria (AC) for this module. For example, for "third-party login," it is necessary to clearly define the AC for all scenarios, such as "first-time authorization binding," "direct login after binding," "authorization cancellation midway," and "expired authorization token," to ensure the team has a unified, unambiguous understanding of expected user behavior and system feedback.
gold: D. The core idea of the speech should focus on source governance of requirements. I would argue that the fundamental way to ensure quality is to ensure the completeness of requirements, providing a clear "target" for development and testing. Therefore, we should re-examine the User Stories and Acceptance Criteria (AC) for this module. For example, for "third-party login," it is necessary to clearly define the AC for all scenarios, such as "first-time authorization binding," "direct login after binding," "authorization cancellation midway," and "expired authorization token," to ensure the team has a unified, unambiguous understanding of expected user behavior and system feedback.

As an algorithm engineer (Weijie Lv), the algorithm models I'm responsible for have been iterating frequently recently. However, after each update, I have to manually run evaluation scripts and check data quality, which is tedious and prone to errors. I hope to automate the evaluation and validation process so that it runs automatically after every code commit, and I receive timely notifications if something goes wrong. I need to plan a solution for this. How should I approach it?

Options:
A. I will follow the latest resolution from the Architecture Committee and use GitLab CI to build a new automated pipeline, seizing this opportunity to promote standardization. According to the "Model Validation and Traceability" section of the "MLOps Best Practices Guide" published by the committee, I will configure the `.gitlab-ci.yml` file. For computationally intensive verification tasks, I will define a `job` that uses a shared GPU runner. At the same time, I will leverage GitLab's `artifact` feature to store evaluation reports and model metrics, and consider registering them with GitLab's Model Registry. Finally, I will configure detailed failure reports to be pushed directly to our project's Slack channel.
B. Although the "Architecture Committee" recently recommended GitLab CI, given that my model project relies on some Jenkins-specific plugins and a complex build environment, the direct migration cost is not low. To achieve quick results, I will temporarily continue using the team's mature Jenkins solution. I will create a new `Jenkinsfile` in the code repository and specify a Python `agent`, then ask my DevOps colleagues to help configure the Jenkins task so that it can be automatically triggered when new code is committed, just like Hanglan Qin did for other projects. This will allow me to immediately utilize automation while planning a complete GitLab CI migration for the next quarter.
C. Considering my work primarily revolves around Python and machine learning models, I would lean towards using GitLab CI, which is more suitable for MLOps scenarios. I would create a `.gitlab-ci.yml` file in my model repository, defining a 'validate' stage. This stage would use a Docker image pre-installed with Python, PyTorch, and related libraries, and execute my validation script (e.g., `pytest tests/validation`) in the `script` section. Finally, I would leverage GitLab's Webhook integration to automatically push alert messages to the team's collaboration channel if the pipeline fails.
D. I would prioritize aligning with the team's existing technology stack. I would first consult the documentation that Hanglan Qin has compiled on Confluence, and then add a new `stage` for model validation in the project's existing `Jenkinsfile`. This `stage` would specify a dedicated `agent` configured with a Python environment, and execute the evaluation script using the `sh 'python run_evaluation.py'` command within the `steps` block. For notifications, I can directly reuse the Slack Notification plugin that Hanglan Qin has already configured to ensure timely alerts in case of failure.

You (Yuping Cheng) have been informed that during the recent UAT for the financial diagnostic application, users reported that the charts in the asset analysis report were a bit difficult to interpret and the information conveyed was not clear enough. Jianguo Huang wants you to prepare some optimization ideas for future iteration planning. How would you respond?

Options:
A. Boss Huang, I'm clear on this issue. At the recent design review meeting led by Director Huilan Chen, a conclusion was reached: simply changing colors is a superficial fix. The team decided to use a more professional "Treemap" instead. I can quickly build a high-fidelity Treemap interactive prototype in Figma, based on our existing Design System, to clearly display the hierarchical structure and proportion of assets. I'll also annotate the new color scheme and interaction instructions, so development can proceed directly from it.
B. Boss Huang, regarding this issue, I've learned there's a more fundamental solution. At last week's design review meeting, chaired by Director Huilan Chen, the team reached a consensus that when there are too many categories or their proportions are too similar, pie charts are not suitable for displaying complex asset compositions and can easily lead to misinterpretations. Therefore, it was decided to deprecate them in the next version. I suggest we directly follow this new direction and use Python's Plotly library to implement an interactive Treemap. This type of chart can not only clearly show the proportion of each major asset class but also intuitively compare sub-items like 'domestic bonds' and 'overseas bonds' through color and area. The information hierarchy is clearer, making it a more professional and thorough solution than simply changing colors.
C. Okay, Boss Huang. This issue can be approached from the perspective of data generation. I will check the Python script that generates the charts and, within the Matplotlib or Seaborn implementation, explicitly assign distinctly different color codes to the 'Domestic Bonds' and 'Overseas Bonds' categories mentioned in the feedback. Alternatively, for a more systematic solution, I will consider replacing the chart's default color palette with a usability-tested, high-contrast palette to ensure the readability of all chart categories from the ground up.
D. Okay, Boss Huang. The most direct way to solve this problem is at the UI level. I can quickly create a solution comparison in Figma, adjusting the colors of 'Domestic Bonds' and 'Overseas Bonds' to highly contrasting colors, for example, using the main brand blue for one and the secondary orange for the other. Then I will provide the new color codes (Hex code) and adjustment instructions to the front-end engineers so they can update them directly in the code.

I (Hanglan Qin) just spoke with Huilan Chen, and the new "Risk Assessment API" has been developed. Currently, our deployment process is entirely manual, which is inefficient and high-risk. She hopes I can propose a reliable automation solution from a responsibility perspective to handle the deployment and subsequent monitoring of this new service. What kind of plan should I submit that would be most suitable?

Options:
A. To improve service observability, I suggest optimizing directly at the application code level. We can customize a deep health check endpoint that reflects the status of downstream dependencies by implementing Spring Boot Actuator's `HealthIndicator` interface. At the same time, we can use Micrometer to add `@Timed` and `@Counted` annotations to key business methods in the Service layer, allowing Prometheus to scrape more granular performance metrics.
B. I suggest writing an Ansible Playbook to achieve end-to-end automated deployment. This Playbook will: 1) use Vault to manage sensitive configurations; 2) pull the latest JAR package from Artifactory; 3) distribute it to the target application server cluster; 4) execute a Rolling Update strategy to avoid service interruption; 5) finally, perform a health check by calling the `/health` endpoint of the API to confirm that the service has successfully started and is available externally.
C. Since the Architecture Review Committee has decided to fully transition to a Knative Serverless architecture, to fundamentally adapt to this event-driven model, I recommend a deep refactoring of this Spring Boot-based service. We can introduce the Quarkus framework as a replacement, leveraging its GraalVM native image (AOT) compilation capabilities to compile the application into a native executable with extremely fast startup times and very low memory consumption. This will fundamentally resolve the cold start performance bottleneck of JVM in a Serverless environment, but it will require development resources to rewrite some code and adjust the architecture.
D. Considering the latest directive issued by the Architecture Review Board this morning, all new non-core services must be migrated to the company's internal Knative platform to optimize resource utilization. Therefore, I recommend using Ansible to orchestrate the entire Serverless deployment process. The specific plan is as follows: First, write a multi-stage Dockerfile to package the application into a lightweight container image and push it to Harbor; then, define a Knative Service YAML manifest, meticulously configuring `minScale` and `maxScale` to achieve on-demand scaling, and integrate Prometheus Operator via Pod Annotations to scrape monitoring metrics; finally, apply this configuration idempotently to the target cluster using Ansible's `k8s` module.
gold: B. I suggest writing an Ansible Playbook to achieve end-to-end automated deployment. This Playbook will: 1) use Vault to manage sensitive configurations; 2) pull the latest JAR package from Artifactory; 3) distribute it to the target application server cluster; 4) execute a Rolling Update strategy to avoid service interruption; 5) finally, perform a health check by calling the `/health` endpoint of the API to confirm that the service has successfully started and is available externally.
